misconceptions.description: Thinking the method of joints can begin at any joint regardless of unknown count
misconceptions.trigger: learner starts at a joint with three or more unknown member forces
misconceptions.feedback: In planar trusses, each joint gives only two equilibrium equations, so you should begin with a joint having no more than two unknown member forces.

misconceptions.description: Treating a negative member force as a mistake instead of a compression result
misconceptions.trigger: learner discards a negative answer as invalid
misconceptions.feedback: If you assumed tension first, a negative value usually means the member is actually in compression.

misconceptions.description: Trying to solve joints before determining support reactions
misconceptions.trigger: learner omits support reactions from the starting joint analysis
misconceptions.feedback: Support reactions are external forces on the truss and must usually be found first so the initial joint equations are solvable.
